properties.name: v0.13.0
properties.notes: Cut 2026-07-25. A minor bump — CLAIMS gains a `seat` property (additive) — with docs/upgrading-to-v0.13.0.md written. THE RELEASE THAT MAKES CONCURRENCY HONEST, and every piece of it came from Anthony's own StoryFlow fleet. (1) A DESIGN KNOWS ITS OWN NAME: an id established on first open in <graph>.id.json, a sibling of the store because the id namespaces every stored key; minted with zero coordination; refused rather than defaulted when unreadable; and a store that already holds a design under the old shared id ADOPTS it, which is what keeps every committed export valid since graph_id is inside the content hash. Two on-disk designs can finally mirror each other. (2) CLAIMS NAME THEIR SESSION and claim_report COMPUTES liveness from the OS: a claim whose session exited is `gone`, listed in `stale` with its note, and excluded from overlaps, because a collision with nobody is not a collision; another machine is `unknown` and still counts. (3) THE LOOP'S SAFETY NET IS PROVEN AND INSTALLED: the nudge path is tested by running the REGISTERED hook command as registered, the server reports installed | absent | broken | unknown, the absence rides the handshake instructions, and reflow2_init now registers the hook it never used to — into .claude/settings.local.json, pointing at the kit so it updates with the package. Manifest: 68 artifacts with frozen cut-time checksums plus cmp:docs, cmp:skills and cmp:claims. Four of the five fleet lessons are now built; req:read-while-held remains blocked on dynograph-storage exposing open_as_secondary.

properties.name: v0.14.0
properties.notes: Cut 2026-07-26. A minor bump — no schema change, nothing breaks, nothing in a consumer repository changes — so no upgrade doc; the version moves because capabilities were added, not because anything is asked of the user. THE RELEASE THAT LETS SEVERAL SESSIONS SHARE ONE DESIGN, INCLUDING ACROSS MACHINES, and the value is in the three cases being told apart rather than blurred. (1) DIFFERENT PROJECTS ON ONE MACHINE never needed anything: each has its own graph directory, so each session runs its own server and they never meet — confirmed by measurement rather than assumed. (2) THE SAME PROJECT ON ONE MACHINE needs a SERVER (--http <addr>), because the store is single-writer PER PROCESS: six processes cannot each open the directory, but one process holding it with six sessions attached still has exactly one writer, so the constraint is satisfied rather than worked around. Underneath: the graph moved Mutex→RwLock so reads stop queueing (and the compiler audited the read/write split for free — all 32 read sites genuinely need only &DesignGraph), and seats are minted per SESSION rather than per process, without which a shared server reports every client as the same owner and claim_report tells six sessions they are each other. (3) THE SAME PROJECT FROM ANOTHER MACHINE additionally needs the host NAMED (--http-allow-host), because the transport answers only requests whose Host header is allowlisted — loopback by default. That is DNS-rebinding protection, and since reflow2 has no authentication it is the only thing between a web page the user visits and their design, so reachability off-box is a deliberate act rather than a side effect of binding a public address. The flag EXTENDS the default rather than replacing it, so naming a remote machine can never lock out the local sessions already on that server; and a reachable bind with no named host now WARNS at startup instead of refusing every remote session with a bare 403 and saying nothing. LIVE SHARING HAS A CENTRE and the docs say so: the machine running the server, which cannot sleep and cannot be offline — so it does not replace the git route for two people working independently. They compose: share live while both are at it, commit and push the export when done. Proven over real HTTP against real servers, with the Host header a remote session actually sends: 9 cases in CI. Manifest: 71 artifacts with frozen cut-time checksums plus cmp:docs, cmp:skills and cmp:claims. THE GATE EARNED ITS KEEP AGAIN — cargo fmt reordered an import after the checksum baseline had been accepted, and the drift was caught rather than shipped.

properties.name: v0.15.0
properties.notes: Cut 2026-07-26, the same day as v0.14.0. A MINOR bump because the schema moved, with docs/upgrading-to-v0.15.0.md written — and the upgrade doc's honest headline is that there is nothing to do. TWO THINGS SHIP. (1) `Verification.method` gains `demonstration` and `observation`, from Anthony's own taxonomy. Test, analysis, inspection and DEMONSTRATION are the four canonical verification methods in DoD and INCOSE practice and reflow2 carried three of them, so 'we showed it working' — which is how a great deal of acceptance actually gets closed — had to be miscoded as a test; `observation` is the as-fielded method, watching a system run without changing it, which is neither inspecting an artifact nor running a contrived example. `review` and `simulation` are KEPT, because removing a value would strand every node carrying it. Additive: an older reflow2 still READS a graph containing the new values — PROVEN by building a binary with the previous value set and pointing it at one — and only refuses to write them, since validation runs on write and the stamp counts node/edge TYPES (unchanged at 28/55). (2) THE v0.14.0 REGRESSION IS FIXED, found the same day it shipped and by hand rather than by any detector: with the graph held AND --http given, the degraded surface was served over STDIO and nothing listened on the port, so every session pointed at that URL got a refused connection — indistinguishable from reflow2 never having been configured, which is exactly the outage req:never-silently-absent exists to end. serve_http is now generic over the service it carries so both arms answer on the transport requested, and the startup line distinguishes the surfaces. The four new cases were MUTATION-CHECKED: reverted against v0.14.0 all four fail with 'nothing ever listened on the port the caller asked for'. ALSO RECORDED THIS CUT, built or not: dec:read-while-held-mechanism DECIDED (a read-only view as of open, not a catchable-up secondary) and req:verification-keeps-up ACCEPTED with cap:verification-freshness planned — the design now knows that a passing check proves only the paths it drives, which is the general form of the bug this release fixes. Manifest: 72 artifacts with frozen cut-time checksums plus cmp:docs, cmp:skills, cmp:claims.

properties.name: v0.16.0
properties.notes: Cut 2026-07-27. A MINOR bump, and the FIRST since v0.11.0 that genuinely locks an older reflow2 OUT: PERFORMED_IN takes the schema from 55 edge types to 56, and the version stamp counts edge TYPES, so a reflow2 older than this refuses a design written by it — loudly, never silently half-read. Machines sharing a graph must upgrade together; docs/upgrading-to-v0.16.0.md leads with that. The enum growth in the same window (Verification.method += demonstration/observation in v0.15.0, Environment.env_type += simulation here) does NOT do this, and the doc says why. THE RELEASE THAT MAKES A PILE OF DOCUMENTS INTO A DESIGN. (1) SP-3b/BL-7 CLOSED after months: `ingest` needed a language model, reflow2 ships no provider, and the calling agent could not be reached mid-run — so the whole extraction pipeline was unreachable from a session. `ingest_step` is the repeated-round collect-then-serve handshake agent.rs had specified since SP-2 and nothing had driven; three or four rounds, NOTHING WRITTEN until the last (prepare rounds replay against a throwaway graph, so an abandoned handshake strands nothing), and NO server-side session state, so it survives a restart and works across seats. (2) It now recovers RATIONALE and TEST EVIDENCE, not requirements alone — and both land unasserted, a recovered Decision `proposed` and a recovered Verification `planned`, because an extraction is an agent's reading of somebody's document rather than the user's signature. Making that safe required tightening unverified_capability to demand a PASSING check: it had skipped on any incoming VERIFIES, so attaching a planned one silenced the question the detect-and-ask skill has always said it should not. (3) NEAR-MATCHES ARE ASKED ABOUT: ingest reads the two thresholds the schema had declared and nothing read, and the band between them reports instead of guessing; a structural token-subset pass catches what scoring cannot, since `Gateway` vs `API Gateway` scores 74 — below any threshold, because ratios fall as length differs. Imported from storyflow, which has fought this for years. (4) BL-95: coverage_report says what the design has never been TOLD ABOUT — every other check reasons about nodes already in the graph, so a design covering a third of a system reported the same `0 open gaps` as one covering all of it. Rolled up and ranked by mass, never a score: an artifact whose location is a directory claims what is beneath it. adopt now ends by asking. (5) req:design-the-simulator ACCEPTED and its first rung built: a check records WHERE it ran, so `proven only in simulation` becomes sayable — the reason for the schema change, since simulating first only pays if you can still tell model from reality afterwards. (6) BL-107: the export lineage chain is now CHECKED by the gate, found because I broke it for six commits while nothing noticed. Manifest: 78 artifacts with frozen cut-time checksums plus cmp:docs, cmp:skills, cmp:claims.

properties.name: v0.17.0
properties.notes:
Cut 2026-07-28. A MINOR bump that locks NOBODY out: no node or edge type was added, so the stamp holds at 28/56 and an older reflow2 still opens a design written by this one — the opposite of v0.16.0, and the upgrade note leads with it. The one real cost is a slow first build, because the dynograph-foundation pin moved v0.11.0 → v0.12.0.

THE RELEASE THAT MADE TWO REPOS CHECK EACH OTHER. Almost everything here was found by running reflow2 against a second real project rather than by reviewing it: dynograph-foundation published its surface, reflow2 composed against it, and each side found defects the other could not see. Three of the fixes are in reflow2 itself, and every one was invisible to inspection and obvious the moment something real ran through it.

(1) A PUBLISHED SURFACE CAN CARRY A PROMISE (req:publishable-promise). export_surface withheld every Requirement as internal, behavioural commitments LIVE in Requirements, so the document offered as 'the published surface' carried structure and no promises. Found when a real provider could not tell a real consumer the one thing it most needed — that a missing store fails loud rather than silently falling back to memory. The promise survived only as a comment in the CONSUMER's build file, on the wrong side of the seam. Requirement.designation fixes it by reusing the mechanism whose semantics were already settled, so every existing check applies unchanged rather than through a second, unchecked channel.

(2) DECLARE WHICH VERSION OF ANOTHER DESIGN YOU DEPEND ON (req:design-dependencies-declared). The trial made it load-bearing: without a recorded pin there is nothing to take a surface AS OF, and the two real consumers sit two minors apart, so an offer from main described neither. Two facts kept apart — what you MEAN to depend on, and what the build ACTUALLY resolves — because storing only one gives either a document that drifts or a fact nothing can contradict. Proven on the real dependency and on a simulated undeclared bump.

(3) TWO DESIGNS ANALYSED TOGETHER without either being written to (compose_and_analyse), and AN INTERFACE THAT PUBLISHES ITS WHOLE CONTRACT (set_interface_spec). The composition's most useful result was a ZERO: with the seam hand-drawn, the ordinary detectors found nothing, which proved they check CONNECTIVITY and not COMPATIBILITY — no ordinary detector compares two nodes' properties across a pair. That measurement is what req:seam-incompatibility now rests on.

(4) THE INSTALL REACHES THE FILE THE AGENT READS. Installing into a repo with no instruction file wrote AGENTS.md, reported success, and stayed invisible to a harness that reads CLAUDE.md first — the same defect class the installer already documented from storyflow, in the opposite direction. The rule is now REACH WHAT READS. The eight slash commands ship with the kit as the one narrow exception to serving everything (dec:commands-are-the-exception), with the single way a command can rot — naming a skill that no longer exists — closed by a lint.

(5) CORROBORATION READS AS CORROBORATION. Recording that one decision QUALIFIES another turned the graph red, because the contradiction detector read the edge type and never alignment. Fixed with both counterweights tested: an opposing edge and an edge that says nothing are still contradictions, so no design written before this release changes meaning.

THE FOUNDATION BUMP WAS NOT HOUSEKEEPING, which AGENTS.md forbids. v0.12.0 closes a type leak reflow2 was structurally exposed to — search_fulltext returned dynograph_text::TextHit, from a crate reflow2 never names and reaches only through an optional feature — and makes the rocksdb and fulltext feature NAMES a committed contract upstream. Verified safe BEFORE the tag existed by building this consumer against the provider's unreleased tree. Migration checked rather than assumed: keys.rs and backend.rs are untouched between the tags, so a graph written by v0.11.0 reads identically.
