{"decision":"UNDECIDED. REFRAMED 2026-07-25 by Anthony, and the reframe is the useful part: what he and his brother were asking for is not a staging GATE, it is a KIND. \"I think I now realize what my brother's idea was trying to say — it is like a brainstorming session where you can work through ideas without committing to anything yet. These would be more like 'ideas' not yet fleshed out and could be held in the graph as just that, 'brainstorming ideas'.\" That dissolves the contradiction this decision was opened over. The git study rejected the index because a gate between every edit and the graph is where intent goes to be forgotten; a brainstorm is the opposite move — the idea DOES enter the graph, immediately, labelled as what it is. Nothing waits outside, so nothing is lost, and the design still never claims a half-formed thought as intent. THE QUESTION THAT REMAINS IS THE VOCABULARY ONE, and dec:edge-orthogonality decides it: a distinction earns its keep only if a computation reads it. So what would read `brainstorm`? The candidates, none of them chosen: gap detection must NOT nag about an idea nobody committed to (an unsatisfied brainstorm is not a hole in the design, and today an unsatisfied Requirement fires forever); delivery and certainty counts must exclude it, or the denominator becomes meaningless; promotion must be an explicit human act — a brainstorm becoming a Requirement is the same signature-forging risk dec:certainty-derived guards, one step earlier; and a brainstorm nobody has touched in months is a candidate for retirement rather than an accusation. If none of those is built, the label is decoration and the honest answer is to keep using `proposed` Decisions the way this session already did for the worktree ideas (dec:concurrent-work-isolation). PRIOR FRAMING, KEPT because it is what was true yesterday: the ask read as an opt-in \"think first, commit later\" mode; what already works is that a session making no write calls IS rubber-ducking, and the read tools are the ducking aids; and the narrow question was what happens at the END of such a session — one deliberate commit, with discarded branches either dropped or preserved as unchosen alternatives under a decision point. That question survives the reframe and is now the second half of it: if ideas land as ideas, the end of a brainstorm is a promotion step, not a commit step.","name":"OPEN — do half-formed ideas get a place in the graph, distinct from things the design asserts?","rationale":"Raised by Anthony and his brother 2026-07-24, reframed by Anthony 2026-07-25 while brainstorming the concurrency ideas — which is itself the evidence for the feature: he produced four options he explicitly did not want to commit to, and the only place to put them was a `proposed` Decision, a node type meant for a choice someone is actually facing. That works, and it is why this is not urgent; it is also a slightly wrong fit, and knowing why is worth recording. Still held proposed because the vocabulary question above is unanswered, and because it may be a SKILL rather than a schema change: a brainstorm skill that records ideas as proposed Decisions and asks before promoting any of them would test the practice without spending a schema change and an upgrade doc on a noun. Anthony's own words put it in that bracket — 'maybe a future skill'.","status":"proposed"}

{"decision":"UNDECIDED, and RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-07-25, explicitly not convinced by the collaboration design and thinking out loud: \"could you have small/mini reflow2 graphs inside itself... coming from a system of systems engineering approach, reflow2 may lay out the graph and how all the systems need to interact and where there are gaps, but what if we now had a mini-reflow2 graph for each system? And a mini-mini-reflow2 of the components in the system... the idea is that reflow2 has the tools to analyze the graph at each level and ensure there are no gaps and that it works with the higher level systems or system-of-systems.\" WHAT IS ALREADY TRUE, because it changes what the idea is asking for. Levels exist and are already checked: Component.level is an enum of component / subsystem / system / system_of_systems / enterprise, CONTAINS between Components is the axis-Y spine, and hierarchy_issues already reports level_mismatch, missing_intermediate_level and orphan_level — the carburetor-to-body problem, imported from chain_reflow's matryoshka insight (docs/three-axes.md). And the multi-graph primitive exists unused: every node and edge carries graph_id, pinned to the constant \"reflow2\". So the question is not whether reflow2 can express nesting. It can. The question is whether a level should be a SUBTREE of one graph or a GRAPH OF ITS OWN. THREE OPTIONS. (a) ONE GRAPH, ZOOM BY LEVEL — today's shape. What is missing is not nesting but SCOPING: no read takes a subtree as its subject, so detect_gaps and graph_report always answer for the whole design. Adding a scope argument is a filter, not an architecture, and it delivers most of what was asked — the tools analysing each level. (b) A GRAPH PER SYSTEM, COMPOSED — Anthony's idea. It buys four things one graph cannot: an independent write lock per system, which is a different and stronger answer to the collaboration problem than region claims, because separate graphs are PHYSICALLY separate where a claim is only advisory; an independent lifecycle, so a subsystem can be released, adopted or handed to a vendor on its own; selective publishing, which is exactly req:design-reachable-without-the-repo; and per-level scale, since detectors run over hundreds of nodes instead of tens of thousands. (c) A GRAPH PER OWNERSHIP BOUNDARY, LEVELS INSIDE EACH — the hybrid, and the shape federated systems engineering actually uses: you split where AUTHORITY splits, not where the hierarchy happens to have a layer. THE FOUR HARD PARTS of (b), each one real: the golden thread cannot cross a store boundary, because the schema validates both endpoints of every edge — so a parent's Component pointing at a child's design needs a typed COORDINATE (graph id + node id + the export's content hash at the moment the reference was made), which is precisely the choice dec:fork-point-address already made for fork points over a native ref layer. Gap detection goes blind at the seam: a parent requirement whose satisfying capability lives in a child graph would fire unsatisfied forever unless the child's evidence rolls up — and that roll-up is cap:derived-completion's computation applied one level higher, which is encouraging rather than novel. Freshness becomes load-bearing: a parent's view of a child is a claim about a VERSION of that child, so it is a dated examined claim and never a live truth (the cap:freshness and confirmation-ledger shape). And the seam becomes the new collision point: two people changing the interface across the boundary still collide, now in the one place with no merge machinery. THE TENSION WORTH KNOWING ABOUT: docs/org-scale-vision.md records the opposite destination — \"one graph the whole company plans in\", with the CEO's objectives at the top and everything tracing upward. Federation and one-big-graph cannot both be the end state, and nothing in the design has ever chosen between them. THE DISCRIMINATOR, offered as a finding and not a decision: depth alone does not justify a separate graph. Nesting three levels of graphs costs a coordinate, a roll-up and a freshness check at every seam, and buys nothing that a scope filter would not have delivered — unless something at that level is separately OWNED, separately RELEASED, or separately SHARED. Where those hold, a graph of its own is right. Where they do not, it is ceremony.","name":"OPEN — one graph with levels, or a graph per system composed into a bigger one?","rationale":"Recorded because Anthony said plainly he is not convinced by the collaboration design, and an unconvinced author is a finding, not a disagreement to be argued down. The three options and the ranking above are analysis offered for him to judge — the brainstorm skill's rule is that a counter-argument is recorded BESIDE an idea rather than used to talk someone out of it, and this decision is the first real test of that rule. Held proposed with nothing built, and deliberately without a Requirement: if federation is the answer it changes the shape of several settled things at once (dec:repo-file-embedded's single file, dec:central-host's hosting question, the whole org-scale destination), and that is a decision to make deliberately rather than to discover halfway through an implementation. The cheap next step, if he wants motion without commitment: add a scope argument to the existing detectors — option (a) — because it is a filter over machinery that already exists, it tests whether per-level analysis is what he actually wants, and it is a strict subset of what option (b) would need anyway, so it forecloses nothing (rule:no-foreclosure).","status":"proposed"}

{"concern":"core","kind":"functional","lineage":"original","name":"The design says which interfaces are the published boundaries, and computations read that distinction","priority":"medium","provenance":"authored","statement":"Some interfaces are the boundary a system is known by; most are internal plumbing. The design must be able to say which — and the distinction must earn its keep by being read, not merely stored (dec:edge-orthogonality). From the MOSA guidebook Anthony supplied (OUSD(R&E), February 2025), whose entire discipline turns on designating modular system interfaces and then holding them stable and open, and independently from BL-45's system-of-systems thread, which found the same hole from the other side: nothing marks an Interface external-facing, so \"visible to others\" versus \"mine to change\" is undeclarable. Two independent routes to one missing property. What must read it, or the designation is decoration: a change that crosses a published boundary is a different risk from one that stays behind it, and impact analysis should say which it is BEFORE the edit; a design that publishes a surface should be able to export exactly that surface and nothing internal; and a composed design (req:design-composes) links through published boundaries, never through another system's internals. What this must NOT become: an assertion that a boundary is stable. Whether a published interface has in fact held is a matter of evidence — its drift history — not a property anyone sets.","status":"accepted"}

{"concern":"core","kind":"functional","lineage":"original","name":"The open structural-defect list means still-needs-attention","priority":"medium","provenance":"authored","statement":"A structural defect that has been reviewed and consciously accepted must move out of the open list into a reviewed one — not deleted, not hidden — the way an acknowledged gap already does. Found as friction 2026-07-25: detect_defects reports the same six findings every run, all six carrying recorded Decisions explaining why they stand, so a genuine seventh would arrive into a list nobody reads carefully and the count is the only signal. reviewed_gaps already keeps this promise for gaps on the stated grounds that \"a list that can never reach zero gets skimmed\"; the defect side makes the same promise in its docs and does not keep it. {"description":"--http <addr> serves the design over streamable HTTP so many client sessions share one process. The store is single-writer PER PROCESS, so this satisfies the constraint rather than working around it: one server means exactly one writer. rmcp builds a service per session through a factory, and ReflowService::share decides the split — the graph and the write generation are shared because they are properties of the design; the seat and the read-hint memory are minted fresh because they are properties of whoever just connected. The graph moved from a Mutex to an RwLock so concurrent reads do not queue behind each other, and the compiler audited the read/write split in the process: all 32 read sites genuinely need only &DesignGraph. No authentication — the flag's help and the startup line both say to bind loopback or a private network.","is_entry_point":false,"is_exit_point":false,"name":"Several sessions work one design at once, through one server","provenance":"authored","status":"verified","tier":"operational"}

{"description":"Both the fifteen skills and the ~20 KB instruction document are compiled in at build time (build.rs embeds getting-started/), served by list_skills, get_skill and get_instructions, and advertised by a catalogue plus a call-get_instructions-first line in the server instructions — the one channel a client puts in the agent's context unasked. {"description":"An id is established on first open and read on every one after, from <graph-path>.id.json — a sibling of the store, because the id namespaces every stored key and so must be known before the design can be read. Minted with zero coordination (creation nanosecond + process + absolute path through fnv1a, no dependency added); the friendly label is a changeable layer on top and never load-bearing. An unreadable identity is REFUSED, never defaulted, because defaulting opens a different design at the same path and reports nothing wrong. THE MIGRATION IS THE FEATURE: a store that already holds a design under the old shared id adopts that id forever, which is what keeps every existing export, chain link and committed record valid — graph_id is inside the export's content hash. properties.name: Brownfield adopt trial on storyflow (2643 files): full RE lifecycle through the adopt skill, 5 true findings about storyflow, 4 about reflow2
A capped read names its cap, its total and where to resume; an oversized single node still returns (tools.rs, 4 cases)

A claim records the session that made it; a claim from a session that exited is a ghost with its note kept; a ghost is not a collision; two live sessions on the same ground still collide; another machine is unknown rather than dead and still counts; a pre-seat claim is unknown rather than assumed live (tests/claims.rs, 6 new cases of 15). Proven end to end over stdio with a genuinely exited server process: gone vs live, zero false overlaps, the ghost named in `stale`.
A claim never blocks anyone, and overlaps are reported rather than prevented

Two designs that both name something `cmp:store` do NOT overwrite each other, and the consumer's design is untouched — the corruption a plain import would cause silently; findings are attributed ours/theirs/seam with a seam finding required to name ids from BOTH sides; composing is READ-ONLY, pinned by the consumer's export content_hash being byte-identical afterwards and carrying none of the dependency's nodes; and an empty namespace is REFUSED rather than allowed to collide by omission (crates/reflow2-core/tests/compose.rs, 5 cases)

An unmodelled subtree is reported and a modelled file is not; ONE OPAQUE ARTIFACT LEGITIMATELY CLAIMS THE MASS BENEATH IT (900 vendored files under a single registered directory report zero unclaimed — the trap a file-count ratio would fall into, since it would score correct coarse modelling as 1-of-901 and call it failure); a shared name prefix does not claim across a directory boundary; exclusions come back NAMED with the rule that excluded them and their mass does not inflate the silence; regions rank by mass so the biggest silence sorts first; a registered location the sweep never mentioned is named; and an empty sweep claims nothing rather than reading as full coverage (crates/reflow2-core/tests/coverage.rs, 7 cases)

The degraded surface comes out of the door the caller asked for: with the graph genuinely held by another process AND --http given, an HTTP client still completes the handshake, still finds the reason in its instructions, and can still call reflow2_unavailable — plus the startup line says DEGRADED rather than letting an operator read 'serving over HTTP' and walk away. 4 cases in tools/test_degraded_server.py, measured against a real held lock. It caught the fault it was written for: against the v0.14.0 code all four fail with 'nothing ever listened on the port the caller asked for', because main.rs's Err arm called serve(stdio()) and never read cli.http (BL-105).

Measured against a REAL held lock: a peer handshakes, the reason arrives in its instructions, one unmistakable tool is served with remedies, a free graph still gets the whole surface — and a held graph exports with the caveat, leaving no residue (tools/test_degraded_server.py, 9 cases)
Delivery is derived from the thread, and goes backwards when the evidence does

A declaration round-trips intact; one without a version is REFUSED because the version is what a surface is taken as-of; a build taking something undeclared is reported (the reliance nobody agreed to); a pin the build has moved past is reported; a declaration the build no longer takes is reported; a feature forwarded by name but never declared is reported; agreement says so plainly; declaring nothing reads as "nobody has said" rather than "depends on nothing"; and the manifest names which reflow2 wrote it, empty or not (crates/reflow2-core/tests/depends.rs, 10 cases). PROVEN ON THE REAL DEPENDENCY: reflow2's actual v0.11.0 pin reconciles with 0 findings, and a simulated undeclared bump to v0.12.0 correctly reports both the version mismatch and the newly-taken crate.

A new design mints a name of its own, it survives reopening, two designs are told apart, an unreadable identity is refused rather than defaulted, the label changes while the id cannot — and the migration case: a store already holding a design under the shared id KEEPS it and stays readable. Closes with the payoff: two independently created ON-DISK designs mirroring each other's published surface, which was impossible while every graph shared one constant (tests/design_identity.rs, 7 cases)
Drift reports which way it went, and names what the design has wrong

An edge to a node that does not exist is refused, not written (found 2026-07-25: authored_by accepted contributor id "person:anthony", which was never created — the edge was stored and get_node returned null for its target, so a phantom AUTHORED_BY sat in the graph until noticed by eye; unwritten)

A capability proven only on a rig says so; ONE real check ends the simulation-only claim (reaching reality must show, since leaving the rig is the point of the progression); a passing check naming no environment is UNPLACED and explicitly not assumed real — unknown is not simulated either; and a capability with nothing passing is absent from the report entirely rather than appearing as proven-nowhere, because that is unverified_capability's question (crates/reflow2-core/tests/evidence.rs, 4 cases)

The ambient agent drives INGEST to completion with no LLM provider, and the design lands with its provenance Fragment; an ABANDONED handshake writes NOTHING (the prepare rounds replay against a throwaway graph, so a half-answered run cannot strand half a design); the same input takes the same rounds, since each call is self-contained and no session state is held; and an answer nothing asked for is reported rather than ignored. 4 Rust cases, plus an end-to-end run over real MCP against the built binary: 4 rounds, 6 nodes, with the recovered Decision and Component both present (crates/reflow2-core/tests/ingest_handshake.rs)

A project with NO instruction file still gets one the primary harness reads; the created file is a pointer, not a second home for instructions (size-bounded); an existing instruction file is appended to, not replaced; a project that already owns a convention gets NOTHING invented; the eight slash commands ship and match the kit source exactly; and SKILLS ARE STILL NOT COPIED, so the exception stays an exception (tools/test_init.py, 6 cases). Plus the guards that make shipping commands safe: a command naming a skill that does not exist FAILS the lint, and the .claude/commands mirror is byte-checked against the kit (tools/skill_lint.py). MUTATION-CHECKED three ways: restoring the only-append behaviour, emptying TREES, and pointing a command at a non-existent skill each fail exactly the check that names them.

A contract records paradigm, payload format, schema, endpoint, operations, auth, transport security and error model; UNRECORDED FIELDS READ AS `unspecified` NOT `none` (the flattering default would tell a consumer an unspecified contract is open); filling one field leaves the others and the name alone, so a spec completed by several people over time loses nothing; an invented enum value is refused rather than stored; and performance limits bind the interface as a Constraint via CONSTRAINS rather than as duplicate properties (crates/reflow2-core/tests/interface_spec.rs, 5 cases)

Published boundaries: internal until designated, a crossing is named, an internal change crosses nothing, standing on a boundary is not crossing it, withdrawal removes it — and the depth-bound bug that reported an unreached boundary (tests/key_interfaces.rs, 8 cases)

The installed kit's manifest agrees with the kit source it claims to be — version, file set and per-file hashes (friction 2026-07-25: reflow2's own manifest is four releases stale and nothing noticed; unwritten)
A KPP breach is computed, an unbound KPP is caught, and an incomplete rollup is not a breach
The confirmed KPP is recordable, and the objective is never invented or mistaken for the threshold (tests/kpp.rs, 3 cases)
latent_mode.rs — an undesigned directory is latent, and a designed one never is

Real git branches: disjoint edits merge with no human, a both-sides conflict leaves the path unmerged and names itself, both additions survive, an unconfigured clone degrades (tools/test_merge_driver.py, 4 cases)

Two designs compose: the mirror carries whose/which-version/when, foreign nodes are marked imported, internals never arrive, the seam is an ordinary local edge reported as a boundary crossing, an id collision is refused with our node untouched, a colliding edge is dropped rather than rewired, and self-mirroring is refused (tests/mirror_surface.rs, 7 cases)

The hook is registered, its script exists, and running the REGISTERED command with a real Stop payload produces the block decision the harness consumes — plus silence when the loop was checked, and once-only firing (tools/test_nudge_path.py, 9 cases). The server's detection covers installed / absent / broken / unmalformed-settings (nudge.rs, 4 cases). FOUND BY WRITING IT: the first version asserted a non-zero exit code and failed against a working hook — Stop hooks block by printing JSON and exiting 0, so the test had encoded the wrong contract.
test_loop_nudge.py — the hook is silent and stateless where no design was started

The surface carries the boundary, its ICD and both sides; nothing internal leaves; the note names what was withheld; an undesignated design gets an EMPTY SURFACE warning; no dangling edges; it does not join the hash chain; and the other side imports it cleanly (tests/surface_export.rs, 7 cases)

A designated promise travels with the surface while undesignated intent stays home and is counted; nothing is published by default; a promise-free surface SAYS it is promise-free and distinguishes "none stated" from "none exist"; a promise count appears in the note; designation can be withdrawn; designating leaves status and statement alone; an invented designation and a non-existent requirement are both refused (crates/reflow2-core/tests/publishable_promise.rs, 9 cases). properties.criteria: PASSING as of 2026-07-24, proven by an automated test, not by an upstream claim. Location: crates/reflow2-core/tests/search.rs, featured arm (`cargo test -p reflow2-core --features fulltext --test search`), three cases. (1) `a_natural_language_question_finds_the_requirement_it_asks_about` — two full questions phrased in a person's own words, each of which shares only some vocabulary with its target, must rank that target first against a distractor sharing common words; pins the CLASS, not the instance. (2) `one_unmatched_word_does_not_erase_a_real_match` — the minimal pin reduced to one variable: `upgrade` matches, and `upgrade zzzznotaword` must still match. (3) `a_question_the_design_does_not_answer_still_returns_nothing` — the other half of the contract, because a disjunction that matched everything would destroy the information content of 'no hits' and bring the duplicate problem back from the other direction. REGRESSION PROOF, the step that makes this more than a decoration: the pins were temporarily reverted to dynograph-foundation v0.10.0 and the suite re-run. Cases (1) and (2) FAILED against the pre-fix build with exactly the reported symptom (SearchResult { hits: [] }) and PASS against v0.11.0; case (3) passes against both, correctly, since AND semantics also refused an unrelated question. A test that passes on the broken build proves nothing, so this was verified rather than assumed. Root cause fixed upstream in dynograph-foundation v0.11.0 (PRs #76, #77): TextIndex::search now matches tokens as a ranked disjunction — at least one token required, BM25 ordering — instead of requiring every token.
